root_cause: Console._write_buffer appended the whole self._buffer to self._record_buffer on every call, whether or not the buffer was actually flushed. Inside console.capture() (_buffer_index > 0) the buffer is not cleared between prints, so each print re-recorded all earlier captured segments (Print1, Print1+2, Print1+2+3, ...), and captured output that never reached the terminal still ended up in the recording.
best_solution: In Console._write_buffer, change `if self.record:` to `if self.record and not self._buffer_index:`. Recording then happens only when the buffer is really flushed to the output file (_buffer_index == 0), the same condition that governs writing. Captured content is never recorded, because capture() takes the buffer away before any flush. That removes the duplicates and makes export_text() show only what was actually printed. The reasoning: the record should mirror what hit the terminal, so it belongs on the same gate as the file write. The old test test_capture_and_record expected captured text to be recorded ('ABC\nHello\n'), so it had to be deleted or rewritten.
acceptable_alternatives: Move the record-extend inside the `if self._buffer_index == 0:` branch just before the write. Any fix where recording happens only on a real flush works. A dedupe that still records captured text (recording only new segments) FAILS, because the hidden test expects export_text() == 'Print 0\n'.
hidden_test_demands:
tests/test_console.py::test_capture_and_record (rewritten; the old version is removed). Console(record=True); print 'Print 0'; inside console.capture() print 'Print 1'..'Print 4'. Asserts capture.get() == 'Print 1
Print 2
Print 3
Print 4
' AND console.export_text() == 'Print 0
', meaning captured output must be left out of the recording entirely. This reverses the old test's expectation ('ABC
Hello
').
locating_signals: The title 'Fix record and capture' points to Console(record=True) plus Console.capture(). grep for _record_buffer.extend leads straight to Console._write_buffer. The function is not named, and the statement is only the title plus an issue link. The issue text (duplicate recording, and a question about whether captured content should be recorded at all) is not in the statement.
our_outcome_summary:
All four configs failed in the Kaggle env (v4/v6/v7/v8 all false). v4 (74s, 55 calls) and v6 (126s, 101 calls) only added repro scripts (reproduce_issue.py, repro_fix.py) and left rich/console.py alone, so the hidden test saw the original duplicated recording 'Print 0
Print 1
Print 1
Print 2
...'. Their repros also assumed captured text SHOULD be recorded (v6 asserted recorded == 'Hello World
'), which is the opposite of the gold semantics. v7 (94s, 44 calls) produced an empty patch. v8 (150s, 54 calls) edited the wrong place: it loosened the `assert self.record` in export_text/export_html to `self.record or self._record_buffer` and never touched _write_buffer. None of them gated recording on _buffer_index.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement is just a title plus an issue link, reproduce the bug first and trace the state that is mutated but not reset: here a buffer that was appended on every call but cleared only under a condition. Put the side effect (recording, logging, caching) behind the same condition as the real output or flush. If the fix changes what an existing test asserts, update that test instead of keeping the old behaviour, because hidden tests are often a rewritten version of that exact test. Always ship a source change, never only a repro script.
